body.statement:
For every data-generating member of
\(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cmp}}(d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max})\),
\(\Pr\{h_{uv}\in\mathcal C_n^h\}\ge1-\alpha\). The claim holds without
selecting a matrix-root branch and without divided-difference or
branch-separation assumptions. If an observed moment law has two compatible
members of the compact class with unequal queried transfers, then the set
need not contract: whenever the common moment pair is in
\(\mathcal C_n^M(\alpha)\), both attained transfers belong to
\(\mathcal C_n^h\).
body.justification: Inverse-image coverage is the globally valid counterpart to local branchwise Wald inference.
body.gap: The cited process-graph inference paper conditions on a differentiable fine-grid effect and does not cover observationally equivalent roots or singular fibers.
body.consumer: Scientific conclusions remain valid when sampling parity, persistence collisions, or finite samples leave several fine-grid causal explanations alive.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a data-generating law \(P_\star\) in the compact stable class, write its fine-grid parameters as \((A_\star,D_\star)\), and denote its stationary coarse moments by \((M_{0\star},M_{1\star})\). Define
\[
 E_n:=\{(M_{0\star},M_{1\star})\in\mathcal C_n^M(\alpha)\}.
\]
The compact-class lower-triangular restriction gives
\[
 \det(\lambda I_d-A_\star)=\prod_{i\in V}\{\lambda-(A_\star)_{ii}\},
\]
so the eigenvalues of \(A_\star\) are its diagonal entries. Its stability-margin restriction therefore implies
\[
 \rho(A_\star)=\max_{i\in V}|(A_\star)_{ii}|
 \leq 1-\gamma<1.
\]
Thus the stability premise of \(\mathrm{lem{:}coarse\mbox{-}law\mbox{-}reduction}\) holds. That lemma gives \(M_{0\star}\succ0\) and
\[
 M_{1\star}=A_\star^mM_{0\star},
 \qquad
 M_{0\star}=A_\star^mM_{0\star}(A_\star^m)^\top
 +\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}A_\star^rD_\star(A_\star^r)^\top.
\]
Membership of \(P_\star\) in the class of \(\mathrm{def{:}compact\mbox{-}class}\) supplies, separately, the lower-triangular zero restrictions, the graph-support zero restrictions, the bounds
\(\max_i|(A_\star)_{ii}|\leq1-\gamma\) and
\(\max_{i,j}|(A_\star)_{ij}|\leq L\), diagonality of \(D_\star\), and
\(d_{\min}I_d\preceq D_\star\preceq d_{\max}I_d\). Hence every defining constraint of \(\mathcal R_n\) in \(\mathrm{def{:}inverse\mbox{-}region}\) is satisfied on \(E_n\), with existential witnesses \((M_0,M_1)=(M_{0\star},M_{1\star})\). Therefore
\[
 E_n\subseteq\{(A_\star,D_\star)\in\mathcal R_n\}.
\]
For \(z\in\mathbb T\), the stability margin gives
\[
 |1-(A_\star)_{vv}z|
 \geq1-|(A_\star)_{vv}||z|
 \geq\gamma>0,
\]
so the queried transfer is well defined. By \(\mathrm{def{:}transfer\mbox{-}confidence\mbox{-}set}\),
\[
 \{(A_\star,D_\star)\in\mathcal R_n\}
 \subseteq
 \left\{z\longmapsto\frac{(A_\star)_{vu}z}
 {1-(A_\star)_{vv}z}\in\mathcal C_n^h\right\}.
\]
Combining the last two inclusions with
\(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}moment\mbox{-}box}\) yields
\[
 P_\star\{h_{uv}\in\mathcal C_n^h\}
 \geq P_\star(E_n)\geq1-\alpha.
\]
Since \(P_\star\) was arbitrary, the bound is uniform over the compact class. The argument tests all defining equations of the inverse region simultaneously; it neither selects a matrix-root branch nor divides by a divided difference.

For the last assertion, suppose that two compact-class members \((A^{(1)},D^{(1)})\) and \((A^{(2)},D^{(2)})\) induce the same stationary coarse moment pair \((M_0,M_1)\), and let their queried transfers be \(h_{uv}^{(1)}\neq h_{uv}^{(2)}\). On the common event
\[
 E_n^{\circ}:=\{(M_0,M_1)\in\mathcal C_n^M(\alpha)\},
\]
the coarse-law identities and the class restrictions, applied once for each \(k\in\{1,2\}\), imply
\[
 (A^{(k)},D^{(k)})\in\mathcal R_n.
\]
The transfer-set definition then gives
\[
 \{h_{uv}^{(1)},h_{uv}^{(2)}\}\subseteq\mathcal C_n^h
 \quad\text{on }E_n^{\circ}.
\]
Thus both unequal, actually attained transfers remain in the confidence set whenever the common moment pair is in the moment box, proving the claimed possible noncontraction.
